candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XXVIII.12. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it'. Ephrem reads the ladder as a Christ-Mary type: the ladder is Christ (Jn 1:51 — 'angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man'), AND the ladder is Mary (because she bridges earth and heaven, bringing God to earth and lifting earth to God). Tewahedo Marian hymnody preserves the Jacob-ladder typology as one of Mary's most prominent OT types, in the Wǝddase Maryam (Praise of Mary).

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XXVIII.17. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven'. Ephrem reads Bethel ('house of God') as the proto-temple, proto-church, proto-tabot. Tewahedo ecclesiology explicitly carries the gate-of-heaven identification through every Tewahedo church: each parish church is in some sense Bethel — a renewed-Jacob place where heaven opens. The Tewahedo qǝddase opens with this consciousness.
